ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $6.90 Ryde voucher refund (NS-7) for the unexempted detour mileage on this RydeTAXI trip; no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride: $44.43 made up of base $3.90, distance $29.53 over 20.94 km, time $8.34, waiting $1.19 and platform $1.47, with no surge [F8][F7]. On a metered service detour mileage passes straight into the fare, so RD-2 applies as a mileage refund rather than the fixed-quote branch [F8][RD-2].

The GPS record settles the deviation: one off-route segment 17:37–17:53 drove 7.60 km where the optimal route covers 2.70 km, adding 4.89 km and reaching up to 1268 m off the optimal route [F4], and the trip overall ran 20.9 km against 15.5 km optimal (+5.4 km, +35%) [F1]. That segment is an unexempted deviation unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [F4][RD-1].

RD-4 gives no excuse. No traffic incident is recorded near the route in the trip window [F15], and the only road-condition facts are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the PIE and CTE, which is not band 1 or 2 and in any event could not exempt a segment on its own [F13][F14][RD-4].

On the rider's stop request the code trace leaves the RD-3/RD-5 reading to me. The rider wrote at 17:33 "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes." [F9], which the driver accepted with "Sure" [F10]. Read in context that is a request for a short stop on the way; it names no road and no outlet, so it is neither a general route authorisation nor a named road or area [F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement is "The rider asked for a 7-Eleven stop. I went to the one I know and waited." [F12] — a driver statement, so under G11 it is not rider consent, and it confirms the driver alone selected the outlet that produced the off-route segment [F12][RD-5]. The rider named no place, so the RD-3(a) exemption does not attach to the driver's chosen outlet 4918 m from pickup [F2]; this is the RD-3(b) situation where a stop was agreed but the driver picked a location that generated the off-route segment [F9][F2][RD-3]. The single segment therefore counts. The chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F11], so this is not an evidence hole: the record settles the meaning of what was said before the segment began [F11][RD-5].

Amount: the unexempted segment's extra_km is 4.89 km [F4] and this trip's per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare over distance km, $29.53 ÷ 20.94 km = $1.4102/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.8959, rounded to $6.90 [F4][F5][RD-2]. The larger billed excess-distance line of $7.71 for 5.47 km [F5] is not refundable beyond the segment: the residual corridor/map-matching mileage that belongs to no measured segment is expressly excluded by RD-2 [F5][F1][RD-2]. The waiting charge is a separate RydeTAXI meter item for 4.6 min at $0.26/min [F6][F8], matching the 4 min 10 s stationary period at the stop [F2]; on a metered taxi waiting units are chargeable and are not refunded [F2][F6][RD-3].

No flag_account: RD-6 conditions a referral on a driver-side finding plus a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, and the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the rider's complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement [F9][F10][F12]; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears, so safety_concern is "none" [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment, the rate, the chat and the fare breakdown are all on the record [F4][F5][F8][F9][F10][F11].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' for 2 minutes without naming any place (F9), and the driver's post-trip statement shows he alone chose the outlet ('I went to the one I know', F12 — a statement, not rider consent, G11), which produced the off-route segment and the stop 4918 m from pickup (F4, F2). No rider message before 17:37 agrees to a route: the complete timestamped chat contains only the 17:33 stop request and the 17:34 'Sure' (F9, F10, F11), which is neither a general route authorisation nor a named road (RD-5). A driver's choice of stop away from the route is not covered by a bare stop request, so under RD-3(b) / RD-5 the segment is unexempted and its 4.89 km extra are refundable at the trip rate of $1.4102/km under RD-2 (F4, F5, RD-1, RD-2, RD-3, RD-5).

rejected_claims.reason: The $1.19 waiting line is a RydeTAXI meter item (F6, F8) for the 4 min 10 s stationary period at the stop (F2). On a metered taxi, waiting units are chargeable and are not refunded under RD-3(c); the outlet location affects only the mileage, which is already refunded under RD-2 (F2, F6, RD-3).
RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days; the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute but route: 0, so the condition fails and no flag_account attaches (F18, RD-6).

Accepted only as to the outcome: with route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 no flag_account is added (F18, RD-6). The claim that the deviation is largely self-inflicted by the rider is rejected: the rider named no place and the driver chose the outlet, which leaves the segment unexempted (F9, F12, RD-3).

The absence of rider consent is correct and is applied, but it does not help the driver: with no exempting clause the segment counts under RD-1/RD-2, and 'undetermined' is unavailable because the record places the segment on the driver's own chosen stop 4918 m from pickup (F4, F2, F12, RD-1, RD-3, RD-5).

The arithmetic basis is correct and adopted (rate $1.4102/km; 4.89 km × $1.4102/km = $6.90), and the corridor/map-matching remainder inside the $7.71 excess-distance line is indeed not refundable under RD-2 (F4, F5, F8, RD-2); the claim is therefore granted, not rejected.
